newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-CWC says may beat BSkyB to digital start.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-CWC says may beat BSkyB to digital start.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Communciations Plc could start digital services before BSkyB gets its satellite project off the ground, chief executive Graham Wallace said on Wednesday.

"We've always said we wanted to be able to launch at the same time as BSkyB and it now looks as if we'll be able to go ahead of them," said Wallace, who heads the British cable telephone and television giant.
BSkyB said earlier that it planned to launch 200-channel digital satellite services into the UK in spring 1998, a few months later than previously planned.

But Wallace said that CWC, which is spending 100 million stg on upgrading for digital, may also wait until spring 1998 before it launches its new services. "We may go at the same time as them in order to create the maximum amount of noise for the whole digital idea," he said in a telephone interview.
BSkyB is joining forces with BT, Midland Bank and Matsushita to offer interactive services to digital viewers.
